sections.body_en:
As in the chapter on Christianity, in this chapter too there is no pretension to encompass the Muslim religion in all its branches, but rather to focus on Judaism's general position regarding it. About one thousand four hundred years ago, close to six hundred years after the founding of the Christian religion, the Muslim religion was founded in the Arabian Peninsula by Muhammad, the prophet of Islam (around [4]390, 630). Its source of inspiration is the Torah of Israel, for the Quran, the foundational Muslim book, is full of ideas from the Tanakh, and through the story of the great figures of Israel, foremost among them Avraham and Moshe, it describes the history of the revelation of faith in God's unity. Muslim law and thought too drew their inspiration from the halakhot and aggadot of the Oral Torah that were transmitted by Jews living in Arab lands. Inspired by Scripture, there was revealed to Muhammad the tremendous power of faith in one God who has no physical presence at all apart from His creating and commanding speech. Beyond the signs and wonders in Scripture, the greatest biblical miracle is the very prophetic speech of God to man: speech that addresses the entire public and sets the goal of establishing a nation of believers, and thereby brings about tremendous changes in the world. Indeed, Muhammad did not perform miracles; rather, in lofty language he expressed the vision of faith, and in speech full of power and momentum he demanded complete devotion to its realisation. The meaning of the word "Islam" is submission, surrender and total devotion to the God who is called "Allah."

Inspired by the faith of Israel, Allah is one, eternal, omnipotent, the Creator of the world who rules it with might, rewarding those faithful to him and punishing those who deny him. Although Islam is free of idolatry, in terms of consciousness it contains a subtle corporealisation. For according to the pure faith of Judaism, God must not be defined by any definition, and all the Divine attributes, such as kindness, might and compassion, are an illumination that is revealed to us, but He Himself is beyond all definition. And although in principle Islam agrees with this, in practice it tends to define Allah according to the attribute of judgement and might, and relates to him as an omnipotent hero, before whom all must submit and whose authority they must accept absolutely.1

Since the main manifestation of Allah is in might, the Muslim believer must gird himself with might and be a soldier in the army of Allah, in order to subdue his evil inclination before him, and in order to fight the unbelievers and subdue them before him. Of the five main mitzvot (pillars) of Islam, four deal directly with honouring God and submitting to him: 1) the declaration of faith in Allah and in Muhammad his prophet; 2) prayer to him five times a day, the essence of which is bowing and accepting the lordship of Allah; 3) fasting on all the days of the month of Ramadan in order to strengthen faith and subdue the evil inclination; 4) the pilgrimage to the city of Mecca in the Arabian Peninsula; 5) "zakat," which is the giving of an annual tax of 2.5% of one's property to the caliph, so that he may fulfil with it God's command, give charity from it to the poor, and lead the jihad to establish the rule of Islam in the world. The giving of zakat must be out of love for God and acceptance of his sovereignty, that all the money is his.

The additional mitzva, which is directed outward, is jihad – holy war against the unbelievers, in order to eradicate idolatry from the world and turn everyone into Muslims, that is, those who submit to Allah, under the rule of the caliph, Muhammad's successor, the leader of the Muslim nation. For this purpose there is a commandment to fight idol worshippers and to present them with the option of converting to Islam or dying by the sword (as detailed in section 4).

notes_en.en: In the view of several Ge'onim, the religion of Islam is idolatry (so it is written in the name of a Gaon in Otzar Ha-ge'onim, Avoda Zara 34a, s.v. "Amar Rav Ḥaviva"; and so it is written in Sefer Ha-eshkol, Yayin Nesekh, p. 150b, in the name of Rav Naḥshon). So wrote Ran on Sanhedrin (61b, s.v. "Yakhol"). However, in the view of the vast majority of poskim, Muslims are not idol worshippers, and their customs around the Ka'ba in Mecca are not considered idolatry (Responsa of Rambam 369). Therefore it was ruled that their wine is permitted for benefit and forbidden for drinking. So wrote Rambam, Hilkhot Ma'akhalot Asurot 11:7; Rema, YD 146:5; Taz, YD 124:6; Shakh 12; see Peninei Halakha, Kashrut 29:3. However, if Muslims force a Jew to convert to Islam in a way that he will not be able to continue keeping the mitzvot of the Torah, he must be killed rather than convert to Islam (Ritva, Radbaz; above 4:7).

sections.body_en:
The most important foundation of faith in Islam is that man must submit to the absolute sovereignty of Allah. This is unlike the Torah of Israel, which, together with the demand for humility before God, also encourages man, who was created in the image of God, to recognise his greatness and the responsibility God has placed upon him, to develop his talents in order to perfect the world and advance it. In Islam, man must accept the world as it is, because that is what Allah wanted, and consequently that is its perfect state, and there is no need at all to repair or change it. All the problems a person has in the world stem from his becoming arrogant and being drawn after his inclinations – stealing and committing adultery, murdering and lying – and not submitting to Allah. If he fights his inclinations with might and restrains them so that he does not sin, all the good and abundance of this world and the next will be laid before him. Since in principle this world is perfect, the Garden of Eden in the World to Come is not essentially different from this world, except that in the World to Come everything is in greater abundance; and after the believer has submitted to Allah in this world, his reward is that he will enjoy in the World to Come all the good there is in the world. Even things that religion forbade him in this world, in order to subdue his inclination, will be given to him in abundance in the World to Come, such as alcohol and many women. (Some Muslim commentators interpret the expressions of physical abundance in Paradise in an abstract way.)

In prayer too, which is among the fundamental mitzvot of Islam, the main thing is submission and praise of Allah. In Israel, the main prayer is the "Amida prayer" (standing prayer), because the one praying must stand before God at his full height and ask God to help him be a partner in bringing God's blessing to the world. For this purpose he asks God for wisdom, healing, economic blessing, the building of Jerusalem and the redemption of Israel. By contrast, in the text of the Muslim prayer there are no requests, but rather repetition of a short formula declaring allegiance to Allah and accepting his rule. Its main element is submission to Allah, expressed in repeated prostrations, in which the face pressed to the ground expresses the believer's readiness to nullify his unique personality before Allah.

In this way the Muslim faith nullifies the uniqueness and autonomy that every creature has, and leaves to man's power of choice one role: to accept the rule of Allah and submit to him. This submission before the Omnipotent gives the Muslim enormous might in his war against his inclination and in his war against the unbelievers. In this way the Muslims conquered many great lands.

The Torah was given to all of Israel at the Sinai revelation, and consequently it belongs to every Jew, and every Jew is commanded to study it and to innovate in it in order to add repair and blessing to the world. So too regarding prophecy: Moshe Rabbeinu is indeed the greatest of the prophets, and a prophet who comes after him is forbidden to dispute the Torah, since it was given to Moshe Rabbeinu before the eyes of all Israel at the Sinai revelation. But the Torah also promised that prophecy would continue in order to direct us to a deeper understanding of the Torah, as befits each generation, and thus the world will continue to progress toward its redemption.

By contrast, in Islam prophecy was given in secret to Muhammad, and the Quran is a sealed Divine book, and Muhammad is a perfect man in whom no error or flaw is possible. He is the seal of the prophets, and therefore his words prevail over all the words of the previous prophets, and there can be no further prophet after him, nor is there any possibility of progressing to a deeper understanding. Therefore there is no room to aspire to future days that will be better; rather, the goal is to imitate what existed in the days of the prophet and his circle. Accordingly, Muslim wisdom does not try to create and innovate, but to arrange systematically all the ideas existing in the world, in order to guide Muslims to overcome the evil inclination and the unbelievers. Within this framework there is an honoured place for law (sharia), which is the Divine law; its observance is more important than the intention of the heart, because it expresses more than anything actual submission to Allah.

Language and speech occupy a central place in Islam, for the whole world was created by the speech of Allah, and wisdom too defines the will of Allah in precise, legal speech. Hence the enormous power of words in Islam, to the point that the argument for proving the truth of the Quran rests on the beauty of its language. Similarly, acceptance of Islam is done through speech. The marriage of a woman or her divorce too is done through speech alone. Muslim philosophy too deals with speech, which is called "kalam." Above all, the word of Allah reaches the world through the speech of the prophet, and from speech comes the inner power of prophecy, which, when it is said in the right and beautiful way, brings reality into being.

Hence the concepts of falsehood and truth in Islam are not as in the rest of the world. Ordinarily, speech is meant to reflect reality, and if it does not reflect it, it is a lie, and by observing reality one can examine whether a person lied or told the truth. But in Islam speech is reality, and therefore a person can say what ought to be as if it already is, for if the speech in itself is right, reality will later turn out to match the speech. As a result, there is an exaggeration of the value of describing reality compared to the value of investigating reality itself, and an exaggeration of the value of rhetorical ability over factual accuracy. Lying is indeed forbidden in Islam, but what is meant is lying for selfish purposes that do not serve the right values.[2] Therefore, when one lies in order to present the unbelievers as wicked, this is not considered a lie but the truth, since it serves the true goal. For the unbelievers too, once they know the truth, will admit that this is what was fitting to say, since Islam is the truth and the unbelievers are the lie. Therefore Muslims tend to describe wars they lost as victories, because that is how it ought to be, and consequently, through right speech, reality will change and in the end they will win. Thus we find that in the eyes of the Jews, the Muslims' struggle against Israel is riddled with blatant lies, but in the eyes of the Muslims they are telling the truth, because that is how it ought to be.

notes_en.en: To those who look at Islam from outside, it seems that according to Islam it is permitted to lie in agreements with unbelievers in order to defeat them (the "Treaty of Hudaybiyya," "taqiyya"); but according to the scholars of Islam, agreements must be kept, and only when the other side violates its part are Muslims permitted to violate it. However, in order to defeat the enemy it is permitted and even desirable to deceive him with sophisticated speech and double meanings; and the enemy, who is not accustomed to the multiplicity of meanings in their spoken language, thinks that they committed themselves to him, but they did not actually lie in the agreement they signed, for had he looked into it deeply he would have understood that they did not commit themselves to what he thought.

sections.body_en:
Since the prominent aspect of Allah is power and might, according to Islam there is a great mitzva to wage holy war against idol worshippers and to present them with the option of converting to Islam or dying by the sword. This is the commandment of jihad, which is meant to eradicate idolatry from the world and establish the rule of Islam over the whole world. Because of the great importance of victory, when there is a clash between accepted law and the way to the Muslims' success and victory, they rule leniently in the law in order to win. This principle exists in Judaism too, but in a much more limited way and for purposes of defence, since Judaism has no aspiration to conquer the world and impose faith by force.

The warriors, who are the representatives and emissaries of Allah, must walk in his ways and fight with enormous might in order to subdue by force those who do not submit to his authority; one who is killed in battle is called a "shahid," from the word for testimony, for by his self-sacrifice he testified to the sovereignty of Allah, and he is promised the greatest reward in Paradise. Around this idea Muhammad succeeded in subduing and uniting all the Arab tribes, eradicating the idols from the religious centre that was in Mecca, and turning it into the centre of the Muslim religion. His tremendous success proved, in the eyes of his believers, the truth of his prophecy. After he died, his successors set out with momentum to conquer the world and make it Muslim. Within thirty years the first caliphs succeeded in conquering all the lands of the Middle East and part of North Africa. In the sixty years that followed, they conquered in the west all of North Africa and Spain, and in the east they reached as far as India.

By the power of this faith the Arabs succeeded in founding a nation of heroic, devoted and stubborn warriors, conquering many lands and imposing Islam on many peoples for more than a thousand years. According to the Muslim conception, the world is divided into two parts: "Dar al-Islam" is the part already conquered by Islam, and "Dar al-Harb" is the place of war, which there is a commandment to conquer and whose inhabitants must be made Muslim; after it is conquered it becomes Muslim consecrated land (waqf), which must under no circumstances be given up. Even if it is conquered from them for hundreds of years, it is still considered consecrated land, which they have a supreme obligation to return to Muslim control. Even when the Muslims are weakened, they are forbidden to give up land that belonged to Islam, for the believer must not submit to any person but to Allah alone. In time of duress, however, Muslims are permitted to sign a temporary ceasefire, and they must strengthen themselves until they can return and conquer the territories that belonged to Islam and continue fighting to establish the rule of Islam over all the inhabitants of the world.

Power and the sword have a central status in the Muslim religion, for they emphasise the actual power of the religion and magnify the greatness and rule of Allah. Therefore the famous slogan "The din (religion) of Muhammad is by the sword" is not a post-facto concession but the ideal. Even when one can hope that over the coming years the conquered will be persuaded to convert to Islam, one should not wait for this; rather, Islam must be imposed by the power of the sword, thereby expressing the absolute sovereignty of Allah. The calls of the muezzin day and night too, from the minaret adjoining the mosque, which towers over the whole surrounding area, whose main purpose is to announce the time of prayer, express the dominion of the religion over the space, toward Muslims and toward others.

In general, thanks to the war against idolatry with all the corruption that accompanies it, Islam advanced its believers morally to act with charity and justice, and to strive to refrain from murder, adultery and robbery. Toward enemies, admittedly, the Muslims acted with cruelty; but all in all, Islam advanced the world morally. For example, in Arab lands women were an economic burden, and when many daughters were born, it was customary to bury the unwanted daughters alive; Islam abolished this custom. Within the framework of blood vengeance it was customary to kill up to forty people for one, and Islam permitted killing only one person. Likewise, lending at interest, which sometimes caused borrowers to be sold as slaves, was forbidden.

Together with the moral progress, the faith position that demands submission suppressed initiative and creative thinking, and in a gradual process that lasted many hundreds of years, it brought about the economic and scientific decline of the states under the rule of Islam. Lands that were considered wealthy relative to the rest of the world deteriorated under the rule of Islam and gradually became backward countries. The oil found in their lands in recent generations does slow the process, but the relative decline compared with the developed countries continues, and it weakens the power of the Muslims, humiliates their religion and arouses their envy.

The faith conception that emphasises the might and rule of Allah also radiates onto the proper form of government in Islam, which is an authoritarian rule that spreads its protection over its subjects, like a compassionate father who cares for the welfare of his children. But everyone knows that his power is great, and when necessary he will cruelly subdue those who rebel against him. Therefore the democratic system struggles to take root in the lands of Islam, because a ruler who is not known to be strong and cruel toward his opponents cannot survive in Muslim culture.

This faith conception, which greatly emphasises the honour of Allah, also influences all interpersonal relationships, which are based on honour. The wife must greatly honour her husband, and the husband, who is the mighty sovereign in his home, must protect his wife and children and provide for them, and this is his honour. Children must uphold the honour of their parents, and then their parents must spread their protection over them and treat them generously. Relations between a person and his fellow too are based on great honour, out of which they arrive at a noble generosity that makes room for warmth and brotherhood. But since honour is very important, an insult shakes the foundations of the soul, and a person who respects himself feels obligated to respond to it with extra severity, to the point that, although Muslim law forbids it, horrific cases of "honour killing" occur. Thus the value of honour, which is fundamentally positive, may turn into an evil inclination of murderous domination within the family, the tribe and the state, and give rise to bloody conflicts.

Unlike Christianity, which grew in the Land of Israel out of Judaism and out of the crisis of the destruction of the Second Temple, Islam grew in the Arabian Peninsula and received its inspiration from Judaism from afar. Out of a simple acceptance of the foundations of faith, reward and punishment in the Tanakh, Muhammad sharply criticised the Jews and argued against them: how, after God chose them from all the peoples, brought them out of Egypt with signs and wonders, split the sea for them, gave them the Torah and bequeathed to them the good land, did they sin against Him greatly and rebel against Him? And however much He punished them and again forgave them, they continued to betray Him, until He brought upon them all the harsh punishments written in the Torah and the Prophets, and punished them with the gravest punishment of all – exile and humiliation.

Following on from this, Muhammad accused the Jews of having falsified parts of Scripture in order to make things easier for themselves, whereas Islam must correct this by absolute acceptance of the commandment at its highest level. Thus Islam took the foundations of halakha in Judaism and gave them an interpretation that is at once simple and powerful. The Jews pray five prayers only on Yom Kippur, whereas the Muslims will pray five prayers every day. The Jews have from the Torah only one fast day a year, Yom Kippur, and the Muslims will have a whole month in which they fast by day and eat by night (Ramadan). In Judaism only one who takes upon himself the vow of a nazir must abstain from drinking wine, whereas Islam decreed that everyone must subdue his inclination and abstain from alcohol. The mitzva written in the Torah, according to which Israel must conquer the Land of Israel and eradicate idolatry from it, the Muslims applied to the whole world. In Judaism there is a mitzva to bow in full prostration only in the Temple, because of the revelation of the Shekhina, whereas the Muslims bow on their faces wherever they pray.

In practice, however, Jewish halakha, with its 613 mitzvot, is far more detailed and binding than Muslim law. For example, the mitzva of resting on Shabbat and festivals does not exist in Islam. The laws of kashrut and family purity in Islam too are very meagre relative to Judaism. The prayer of the Muslims too is much shorter than the prayer of the Jews, so that the five prayers the Muslims pray each day last about a third of the three Jewish prayers. In general, Islam is stringent in mitzvot that express submission to God, but in the overall body of mitzvot it is very lenient. In Islam there is even contempt for the Jews for the many mitzvot they have. In practice, the reduced legal demands in Islam enabled the Muslims to focus on establishing a nation of warriors loyal to the religion.3

notes_en.en: Jewish halakha encompasses all of human life, because the aim of Judaism is to elevate life in all its components, including also the creative power in man, which too is the will of God. For this purpose the Divine command encompasses all areas of life, and it elevates and refines them all in order to bring redemption to the world. But as great as the all-embracing challenge is, so great is the difficulty of realising it, and all the crises that our people has undergone are stages on the long and difficult road to the redemption and repair of the world.

sections.body_en:
At first Muhammad hoped that the Jews would accept his message and thereby crown Islam as the true religion continuing the Divine revelations of the Torah. But when they refused, he saw their refusal as a continuation of their rebellion against God, became their enemy, and held that it was Allah's will that they be severely punished and humiliated for having rebelled against him.

In general, Muslim law distinguishes between idol worshippers, who must be killed if they do not convert to Islam, and Jews and Christians, who are the peoples of the Book, holding holy scriptures given from the mouth of Allah, and therefore must not be killed if they do not convert to Islam. However, they must be punished and humiliated for not accepting Islam. This includes paying a high poll tax every year, accompanied by an act of humiliation. Likewise, they were forbidden to ride a horse, to carry a sword, to build houses higher than the houses of Muslims, and to display their faith and religion outwardly. Although in principle Christians and Jews have equal status, the attitude of the Muslims toward the Jews is harsher, since in their view the Jews rebelled against Allah and it is his will that they be punished.4

According to Muslim law, as long as the Jews pay their taxes and accept their lowly status, they must not be killed and their property must not be plundered. In practice, however, from time to time, following outbursts of religious fanaticism, many cases of severe persecution of the Jews occurred throughout the Muslim realm, including murder, forced conversion, abduction of women and children and plunder of property. Compared with the lives of Jews in Christian countries, under Islam there were fewer violent outbursts, since in Islam the law has supreme status; therefore, on the one hand they were more careful about humiliating and oppressing the Jews, and on the other hand there were fewer cases of violent outbursts. Whereas in Christian society, although Christian law determines that Jews must not be killed or forced to change their religion, since the law is less important, on the one hand there were many more cases of severe outbursts of murder and plunder, and on the other hand there were also more periods in which Jews were allowed to establish themselves and contribute their talents to the economic and scientific development of the European continent. The result was that, all in all, although in Christian lands there were more persecutions and pogroms, the Jews there multiplied and grew wealthier more than the Jews under the regime of oppression and humiliation in the lands of Islam.5

All in all, in Muslim lands the Jews suffered for many generations from oppression and humiliation, and at times from pogroms and murder, until it seemed that there was no more hope for Israel. As a result, there were Jews who did not withstand the test and converted to Islam. But many continued to believe in the Lord, the God of their fathers, who had not broken His covenant with them, and believed that all their sufferings were sufferings of love, in order to refine them and arouse them to strengthen themselves in Torah and mitzvot. Every morning and evening they remembered the Exodus from Egypt and the miracles God performed for Israel, and in this spirit they prayed for the redemption and the ingathering of the exiles, for the building of Jerusalem and the restoration of the kingship of the House of David. And with weeping they prayed and confessed: "We have become more ashamed than any nation; joy has departed from us; our heart is sick through our sins… The abode of our Sanctuary is destroyed through our iniquities, our palace has become a desolation, the beauty of our land belongs to strangers, our strength to foreigners." "We are astonished at the evils, our strength is weakened by troubles, we are bowed down exceedingly, we are brought low to the dust…" "O Lord, hear Your needy ones who entreat Your presence; our Father, do not hide Your ear from Your children." "Our Father, merciful Father, show us a sign for good and gather our dispersed from the four corners of the earth. Let all the nations recognise and know that You, Lord, are our Father… Look, please, and save, please, the flock of Your pasture" (from the prayers of Taḥanun and the Seliḥot).

notes_en.en: Regarding the attitude toward the Tanakh, the Christians have an advantage, for the Muslims accuse the Jews of having falsified the Tanakh according to their needs, whereas the Christians believe that the Tanakh is holy and therefore draw inspiration from it. So ruled Rambam (Responsa of Rambam 149): it is permitted to teach Torah and mitzvot to Christians, since they believe in the sanctity of the Torah given from Heaven; and although they interpret the Torah improperly, since they believe in its sanctity, there is a possibility that they will return to the right path through the study. And even if they do not return to the right path, no stumbling block will be caused by it. But it is forbidden to teach Torah and mitzvot to Muslims, since they do not believe in the truth of the Torah, and there is a concern that they will use what they learn for evil and against Israel; and to them and their like applies the prohibition against teaching Torah to a non-Jew (Ḥagiga 11a; Sanhedrin 59a).

We shall mention some of the pogroms that the Jews endured under the rule of Islam: already in the days of Muhammad, following the Jews' refusal to join Islam, the Muslims robbed and murdered many Jews. In the year 4793 (1033), more than 6,000 Jews were murdered in Fez in Morocco. On 9 Tevet 4827 (1066), more than 4,000 Jews of the Granada community were murdered, headed by Rabbi Yehosef Ha-nagid, adviser to the king. From the year 4892 (1132), the Almohad (al-Muwahhidun) movement began to rule North Africa and Muslim Spain for close to a hundred years; they placed before the Jews a choice between death, conversion to Islam or expulsion. As a result of their decrees, the many important Jewish communities under their rule were destroyed. In this context many Jews were also murdered, and not a few converted to Islam under coercion. In the year 5225 (1465), thousands of the Jews of Fez were murdered; only 11 survived. In [5]336 (1576), they murdered and plundered the Jews of Marrakesh and finally expelled them all. There were many more pogroms and expulsions in the communities of Morocco. In the modern era, when there was not enough money to pay the soldiers, they would organise pogroms against the Jews and pay the soldiers with the plunder. The most famous of these is the "Tritel" in [5]672 (1912) in Fez. In Yemen too there were many persecutions, the gravest of them in the year [5]440 (1680), the "Mawza Exile," in which they had to choose between converting to Islam or expulsion; following the refusal of the overwhelming majority of the Jews to convert to Islam, they were expelled from their cities to a desolate region. Some estimate that as a result about two-thirds of the Jews of Yemen perished. Likewise, in the modern era there were two periods in which a law was established that young orphan boys and girls be forcibly converted to Islam. In Persia, under persecution and murder, the Jews of Isfahan were forcibly converted to Islam and lived as anusim (forced converts) between the years [5]382-[5]389 (1622-1629); and again in [5]415 (1655) they forced the Jews of Isfahan, and after them the Jews of Kashan and Hamadan, to convert to Islam while destroying the synagogues. At that time the Jews of Shiraz were expelled from their city to the desert. The pogroms were accompanied by murders and torture of rabbis and elders, children and women, and in the course of this the stories of kiddush Hashem multiplied. In the year [5]599 (1839), under pogroms of murder, the Jews of Mashhad were forced to convert to Islam; some of them fled and most lived as anusim for several generations. In general, about five hundred years ago the Persians became Shi'ites, and since then the Jews of Persia have suffered from persecutions and humiliations. In parallel, throughout the Middle East under the rule of the Ottoman Empire, the laws were better upheld, and as a result the pogroms decreased.

sections.body_en:
In recent generations God has seen the affliction of His people and given strength to those who immigrated to the Land to take hold of it and build it, until we merited, by God's kindness, to establish the State of Israel. But at the same time great fury arose in the Muslim world against Israel and against the Jews. The Muslim religion requires humiliating the Jews and thereby proving that it has inherited [the place of] Judaism, whereas the return of the Jews to conducting themselves as masters is considered defiance against Islam. Not only that, but the State of Israel arose on land that was conquered by the Muslims one thousand three hundred years earlier, and since then, in their conception, it is considered Muslim consecrated land, and they are obligated to destroy the State of Israel and return its land to Islam (see above section 4).

On the strength of this position, Muslim religious scholars determined that every Muslim is obligated to fight the State of Israel and destroy it, and not a few even expressed fierce hatred for all Jews and longed for their annihilation. There are Muslim religious scholars who recognised the power of the State of Israel and agreed that as long as the Muslims do not have the power to defeat Israel, the obligation is not to fight the State of Israel but to act to weaken it from within and without, and to wait for the opportune moment when they will be able to fulfil their obligation to fight the State of Israel and destroy it. The various mediators between the Arabs and Israel propose compromise proposals, but they do not understand that, unlike the conception accepted in the world, according to which it is sometimes right to make compromises, according to Islam there is no room for compromise on the principles of religion. For compromise expresses weakness and is utterly contrary to the Muslim's obligation to represent the power and might of Allah and to hold the sword in order to establish the rule of the religion of Islam. Only when it is clear that there is no possibility for the Muslims to win are they temporarily exempt from the obligation of war. And then their obligation is to educate their children that even if a hundred years pass in which they cannot conquer the State of Israel, they must not give up their aspiration to grow strong and destroy it, and to punish the Jews who offended their honour. Thus Israel and the Jews of the world find themselves in a hard and prolonged war with Islam. The stronger and more determined the State of Israel is, the more Muslims will find themselves exempt from the obligation to fight Israel and the Jews; and the less strong it appears, the more Muslims will think it can be defeated, and will see themselves obligated to fight it in order to destroy it.

But perhaps an opening of hope can be found. There are expressions in the Quran of respect for the Children of Israel who will return to the Land of Israel. And there are Muslim commentators who hold that there is a difference between the expression "Jews," which is directed at the Jews who betray God, and "Children of Israel," who are faithful to God and entitled to inherit the land He bequeathed to them. There are also a few but important Muslim scholars who hold that the emphasis on war, which leads to murder and terror, is a mistake, and that in truth the purpose of Islam is to add peace, love and compassion to the world, to call for an inner jihad against the evil inclination, and to educate toward giving honour to all creatures instead of belligerence.

May it be God's will that the position of the Muslims who respect the Jewish people prevail, and that they merit to purify Islam of hatred of Israel and cleanse it of the inclination to pride and murderousness. Thanks to a positive attitude toward Judaism, they will be able to learn, according to their own way, that creativity and initiative too are a Divine creation that God created in man, and they will free Islam from the stagnation that has clung to it out of an exaggeration of the value of submission, which stifles human creativity and initiative, and thereby bring blessing and prosperity to their peoples. In this way they will be able to impart to the world important values that were developed in Islam, such as the value of honour, which is lacking in the modern world. Through the elevation of the value of freedom, in Western countries excessive freedom has been given to the strong and the rich to lord it over different people and to disparage their values. Restoring the value of honour toward Heaven and honour toward fellow creatures can heal some of the ills of the modern world, add depth and meaning to human life, and make it more moral and better.
